title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 spec Release Candidate lands — stateless core + MCP Apps + Tasks + Extensions
bullets.summary: The RC (final ships Jul 28) drops the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header so every request is self-contained, adds a first-class Extensions framework, a Tasks lifecycle for long-running server-directed jobs, and MCP Apps that let servers ship sandboxed interactive HTML UIs over the same JSON-RPC consent path.
bullets.how: A structural change to the substrate the whole MCP fleet runs on; stateless simplifies our connector orchestration and Tasks/MCP-Apps map onto how agents run long jobs and render dashboards. Audit each server against the six breaking changes before Jul 28; eye MCP Apps as a native replacement for hand-built dashboard panels.

bullets.title: Anthropic ships MCP Tunnels as a Research Preview — reach MCP servers inside private networks
bullets.summary: Connect Claude to MCP servers behind a firewall / on a private LAN without exposing them publicly, alongside Sonnet 5's promotional $2/$10 per-Mtok pricing through Aug 31.
bullets.how: The Construct runs local services (V4 dashboard on 10.1.10.195:8081, Hermes, internal repos); tunnels are the sanctioned path to wire private/on-prem tooling into the fleet instead of pushing everything to public endpoints. Pilot against one internal service before leaning on it for client work.

bullets.title: Frontier model shuffle: GPT-5.6 hits GA as ChatGPT's default; Grok 4.5 tops agentic tool-use but hallucinates more; Gemini 3.5 Pro slips
bullets.summary: OpenAI opened GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) to GA Jul 9 and made it ChatGPT's default; Grok 4.5 (Jul 8) ranked #4 on Artificial Analysis with the best agentic tool-use score but hallucination jumped 25%->54%; Gemini 3.5 Pro remains in limited Vertex preview, ~6 weeks late.
bullets.how: Pure routing-layer input: GPT-5.6 is a fresh default to bench; Grok 4.5 is tempting for tool-heavy loops but the 54% hallucination rate makes it unsafe for anything unverified. Keep provider-agnostic routing so each is a config change; gate high-hallucination models behind verification steps.

bullets.title: Prime Intellect raises $130M Series A to help enterprises build their own AI agents
bullets.summary: Announced Jul 8; the round funds tooling for enterprises to stand up in-house agent stacks rather than buy off-the-shelf.
bullets.how: A PRAGMA market signal: capital is flowing into 'build-your-own-agent' enablement, validating the AI-operator consulting thesis and naming a DIY-tooling category PRAGMA will be measured against. Position PRAGMA as the operator layer on top (strategy, orchestration, owned MCPs), not a competitor to raw agent-builder tooling.

bullets.title: arXiv: "From Question Answering to Task Completion — A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design"
bullets.summary: Surveys how agent 'harnesses' (memory, tools, control flow, verification) determine task-completion reliability, moving the frame from model quality to system design.
bullets.how: Our edge is the harness (CLAUDE.md locked rules, agent memories, connector registry, verification steps), not the base model. Use the survey's taxonomy to find harness gaps — especially verification and failure-recovery — and treat harness design as the durable moat as base models commoditize.

praxis_lesson: Today's signal was infrastructure, not headlines — the MCP protocol itself is going stateless (Jul 28) and Anthropic shipped tunnels to reach private servers, both of which change how The Construct's connector fleet is wired rather than what any single agent can do. The move: harden the plumbing (audit servers against the RC's breaking changes, pilot tunnels for our on-prem services) and keep the durable edge in the harness — memory, orchestration, verification — while treating frontier-model churn (GPT-5.6 GA, Grok 4.5's 54% hallucination rate) as swappable config behind provider-agnostic routing.
